criterion_notes.c1: Fails C1 (Exclusion Criterion 7: water-resource studies unrelated to household or community service access). The article focuses on upstream watershed and recharge-area land-use protection for the Guacerique watershed and Los Laureles reservoir in Tegucigalpa, explicitly contrasting neglected watershed stewardship against downstream efforts to expand water supply coverage to consumers.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording vs. narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: Under the plain broad wording of Criterion 2, the paper discusses legal, institutional, and governance factors (unapplied Protected Forestry Zone and restricted-development laws, fragmented mandates across SANAA, COHDEFOR, and environmental ministries, and IMF austerity/privatization pressures cutting SANAA's watershed management unit), though these concern catchment land-use protection rather than service access. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading, C2 is 'no' because none of the analysed legal or institutional factors is a rule-type mechanism directly governing household or community water/sanitation service access (background mentions of flat monthly fees and national coverage rates are descriptive context only). Even under the plain wording of C2, the overall decision remains 'exclude' due to failing C1, C3, C4, and C5.
criterion_notes.c3: Fails C3. The article is a narrative policy and case-overview essay drawing on secondary technical reports and general literature (9 references total), with no empirical methodology, primary data collection, or systematic synthesis reported.
criterion_notes.c4: Fails C4. Outcomes discussed are biophysical and operational source-water metrics (hillslope erosion, reservoir siltation/carryover storage loss, algal blooms, raw-water turbidity and coliform counts, and chemical treatment costs), rather than household or community water or sanitation service access, connection, continuity, or affordability outcomes (aside from citing aggregate national UNDP coverage figures as background).
criterion_notes.c5: Fails C5. There is no identifiable empirical study design, household/community sample, or analysed service-access exposure-outcome relationship; the unit of discussion is a municipal watershed/reservoir system in a narrative overview.

evidence_quotes.quote: For a variety of reasons, geographical and economic, watersheds like Gaucerique may frequently become neglected components of the water supply system and their protection receive much lower priority than efforts to expand and improve water supply coverage to consumers.

Prior to the opening of the Los Laureles reservoir in 1974, the Honduran government declared the whole watershed as a Protected Forestry Zone in January 1973, a status that remained on the statutes throughout the period in which the changes in the watershed described herein took place.

The situation in Tegucigalpa clearly brings into focus the biophysical implications of the failure to coordinate national and municipal policies in managing and protecting the watershed, and the legal and institutional impediments that have given rise to this situation.

Average erosion rates from hillslopes have been estimated conservatively to cause a loss of more than 200,000 m3/year of carryover storage from siltation, or more than 2 percent of its volume annually, with some feeling that this could be an underestimate, although no formal study has been completed.

raw_response.exposure: Urban land-use expansion, uncoordinated government development projects, weak enforcement of watershed/forestry protection laws, and austerity cuts to SANAA's watershed management unit
raw_response.outcome: Watershed degradation, reservoir sedimentation and storage volume loss, raw-water contamination/turbidity, and elevated municipal water treatment costs (no household or community service access outcome)
raw_response.population_and_sample: Guacerique watershed and Los Laureles reservoir in Tegucigalpa, Honduras (no empirical sample reported)
raw_response.rationale: Excluded as E01 (Wrong topic; Exclusion Criterion 7: water-resource studies unrelated to household or community service access). Lee (2000) is a non-empirical narrative policy/case overview of upstream watershed degradation, land-use regulation failures, and institutional neglect of catchment stewardship around the Guacerique watershed and Los Laureles reservoir in Tegucigalpa, Honduras. It does not examine household or community water or sanitation service access, analyses no rule-type legal/administrative mechanism governing service access, reports no empirical study design or primary data (also failing C3), and measures no household/community access outcome.
raw_response.study_design: Narrative policy and case overview (non-empirical essay)
